history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Sikh gurdwara, keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV TOWN AND DISTRICT BOTH WRONG: there is no Gurudwara Bhatta Sahib in Moga; the famous shrine of this name is at Kotla Nihang on the outskirts of Rupnagar (Ropar), on the bank of the Sutlej. After leaving Anandpur Sahib in 1705 and pursued by Mughal forces, Guru Gobind Singh Ji asked the Pathans of Kotla Nihang for shelter; they jestingly pointed to a burning brick kiln (bhatta) as the only fit place. The Guru led his horse to the kiln and the fire miraculously went out. The present gurdwara was built at the kiln site by Baba Jiwan Singh in 1914. Preserved here are a silver sword, katar and dhal gifted by the Guru to the Pathans. A fair is held on 11 Bhadon (August) marking Baba Jiwan Singh's death anniversary, and another on 2-4 Poh (December).

name: Gurudwara Bhatta Sahib
town_description: Rupnagar (Ropar) is an ancient city on the banks of the Sutlej in Punjab, 42 km from Chandigarh. It is the first Harappan site excavated in independent India, sits below the Shivalik hills, and is known for Anandpur Sahib, the Sirhind Canal and the Bhatta Sahib gurdwara.

travel.road: At Kotla Nihang on the Ropar-Nangal road (NH 205); accessible by bus or auto from Rupnagar

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; fairs in August and December draw large sangat
